parts.label: a
parts.technique: Calculating S_tt and S_gt from summary statistics
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly gives the S_xx formula and its use from summary statistics; this is standard summary statistic calculation, not the PMCC formula itself.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Calculating PMCC from S_tt, S_gt, S_gg (using formula)
parts.reason: S5.1 explicitly excludes calculation of correlation coefficients using the formula ('use of the formula is not required'); here the formula is required using summary statistics, matching the exclusion.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Informal interpretation of correlation between two variables
parts.reason: S2.2 covers informal interpretation of correlation; no calculation required, just reasoning about direction of correlation.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Discrete probability distribution / cumulative distribution function
parts.reason: S4.1 covers discrete probability distributions; finding constant k in a cdf is part of working with such distributions, not excluded (exclusion is only mean/variance calculation).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding probability distribution from cdf
parts.reason: Same as above, S4.1 covers discrete distributions generally, this is standard manipulation not excluded.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Var(aX+b) using given Var(X) for discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables'; this part requires manipulating variance of a discrete RV (even though a value is given, the required method is a variance transformation for a discrete RV), matching the exclusion.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Calculating S_tm for regression line
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly excludes calculations involving regression lines; this is a direct step in constructing a regression line.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding regression line equation
parts.reason: S2.2 explicit exclusion: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Using regression line to estimate value
parts.reason: Uses the regression line from the excluded part (b); calculation involving regression line, excluded by S2.2.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Commenting on reliability of regression estimate (interpolation/extrapolation)
parts.reason: Although S2.2 mentions interpolation/extrapolation danger conceptually, this part depends on the excluded regression calculation in (b)/(c), so is OUT as it only makes sense after excluded work.

parts.label: b

parts.reason: S4.2 covers use of Normal distribution to find probabilities/values, consistent with calculator use for normal distribution.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Conditional probability with Normal distribution
parts.reason: S3.2 covers conditional probability formula generally, and S4.2 covers normal probability calculations; combining them is standard application, no exclusion applies.

parts.label: a

parts.reason: S2.1 explicitly covers histograms where area represents frequency.

parts.label: b

parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly states use of linear interpolation to calculate percentiles from grouped data is expected.

parts.label: c

parts.reason: S2.3 covers calculation of standard deviation including from summary statistics, and mean is a measure of central tendency covered.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Skewness measure calculation and interpretation
parts.reason: No statement mentions skewness; S2.3 lists only mean, median, mode, variance, sd, range, IPR as measures - skewness is a distinct named concept not covered, so out per the 'named concept not mentioned' rule.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: S4.2 covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Comment referencing skewness and normal distribution fit
parts.reason: This part explicitly requires reference to the skewness result from part (d), which is out of spec; since it only makes sense after an out-of-spec part, it is OUT.
